title: Chapter 11 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of AWS pricing models, Free Tier management, budgets, tags, and cost optimization.

questions.question: Which pricing model provides the highest discount but with the risk of instance termination?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% discount but can be terminated by AWS with a 2‑minute warning.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of a Compute Savings Plan over a Standard Reserved Instance?
options: Applies automatically to any EC2 instance family, size, or region
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans provide flexibility to change instance types, families, and regions while retaining the discount.

questions.question: When does the AWS 12‑Month Free Tier expire?
options: 12 months after you launch your first EC2 instance
questions.explanation: The clock starts on the day you create the AWS account, regardless of when you start using services.

questions.question: Which of the following resources incurs a cost even when not actively used?
questions.explanation: Elastic IPs cost a small hourly fee when not associated with a running instance.

questions.question: Data transfer between AWS regions is always free.
questions.explanation: False. Outbound data transfer between regions is charged per GB, typically at the internet data transfer rate.

questions.question: Which AWS Budget type tracks whether your Reserved Instances are being fully used?
questions.explanation: Reservation budgets monitor RI utilization and coverage to ensure you're not wasting reserved capacity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of AWS Cost Allocation Tags?
options: To track costs by custom categories like department or project
questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags allow you to organize and track AWS costs by meaningful categories in billing reports.

questions.question: After creating a user-defined tag, what must you do to see it in Cost Explorer?
options: Activate it for cost allocation in the Billing console
Apply it to at least 10 resources
questions.explanation: Tags must be activated in the Cost Allocation Tags section before they appear in cost reports.

questions.question: What is consolidated billing in AWS Organizations?
options: Combining usage across multiple accounts to reach volume discounts and one bill
Using a single credit card for all purchases
questions.explanation: Consolidated billing allows a management account to pay for all member accounts and aggregate usage for volume discounts.

questions.question: Which AWS tool provides detailed, hourly line‑item billing data in CSV format?
questions.explanation: The CUR delivers the most granular billing data, including tags and resource IDs, to an S3 bucket.

questions.question: What does the Compute Optimizer do?
options: Recommends optimal EC2 instance types based on utilization metrics
questions.explanation: Compute Optimizer uses ML to analyse configuration and utilization and recommend better instance types.

questions.question: Which S3 feature helps reduce storage costs by automatically moving objects to cheaper tiers based on access patterns?
questions.explanation: Intelligent‑Tiering monitors access patterns and moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers automatically.

questions.question: What is a zombie resource in AWS cost management?
options: A resource that is running but no longer needed or unused (e.g., unattached EBS volume)
A resource in a stopped state
questions.explanation: Zombie resources are still incurring charges but serve no purpose. Examples: orphaned EBS volumes, idle load balancers.

questions.question: Which AWS service can prevent non‑production accounts from launching expensive instance types?
questions.explanation: SCPs in AWS Organizations can set permission guardrails, such as denying access to large instance types.

questions.question: What is a common cost‑saving practice with EC2 Auto Scaling?
options: Use scheduled scaling to reduce capacity during off‑peak hours
Disable scaling to keep costs constant
questions.explanation: Scheduled scaling allows you to scale in during nights or weekends, saving costs without compromising availability.

questions.question: The AWS Free Tier includes unlimited data transfer out of AWS.
questions.explanation: False. The Free Tier includes 1 GB of data transfer out per month; beyond that, standard rates apply.

questions.question: Which of the following is a tip to stay within the Free Tier?
options: Run as many instances as you want if they are t2.micro
Set a zero‑spend budget to alert when any cost is detected
Use Elastic IPs on all instances
Store as much data as you want in S3
questions.explanation: A zero‑spend budget sends an email the moment any cost accrues, helping catch accidental usage.

questions.question: What does AWS Cost Anomaly Detection do?
options: Stops resources when cost exceeds a limit
Uses machine learning to detect unusual spending patterns and alert you
questions.explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection learns your normal spend and alerts on unexpected spikes without static thresholds.

questions.question: You need to split the AWS bill across departments based on usage. Which approach is best?
options: Use separate AWS accounts without consolidation
Use cost allocation tags and separate accounts with consolidated billing
Manually divide the total bill by the number of departments
Assign each department a separate credit card
questions.explanation: Tags provide granular tracking; consolidated billing gives a single bill while maintaining account separation.

questions.question: Which of the following can help reduce RDS costs?
options: Use reserved instances or Savings Plans for steady workloads
Always use the largest instance size
questions.explanation: Committing to a 1‑ or 3‑year term with RIs/Savings Plans provides significant discounts for predictable database workloads.
